response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Replace the flag helper that always returns false with an explicit disable or a real gate

Affected:
- pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200
- pkg/expr/reader.go:129-132

Explanation:
`enableSqlExpressions` returns `false` on both branches, so `FlagSqlExpressions` has no effect. SQL expressions are rejected even when the flag is on.

The local variable makes this worse. `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` is true when the flag is *off*, which is the opposite of its name. Readers will assume the flag controls the feature when it does not.

This causes three problems:
- **Unclear intent.** If the goal is to gate on the flag, this is a bug, because flag-enabled users are still rejected. If the goal is a hard disable while the DuckDB engine is gone, the flag lookup is dead code that hides that decision.
- **Risk of accidental re-enable.** A later "fix" to this function could quietly turn the feature back on while the `sql.DB` backend is still a stub.
- **Untestable behavior.** Because the result is constant, no test can tell "flag on" apart from "flag off".

Make the intent explicit.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
// SQL expressions are temporarily disabled regardless of feature flag
// (go-duck backend removed). TODO: restore flag gating when an engine exists.
func enableSqlExpressions(_ *ExpressionQueryReader) bool {
	return false
}

// or, if gating on the flag is intended:
// func enableSqlExpressions(h *ExpressionQueryReader) bool {
// 	return h.features != nil && h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
// }
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Update existing SQL expression tests, since every SQL path now errors

Affected:
- pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-22
- pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:22-26
- pkg/expr/sql_command.go:96-100

Explanation:
`NewInMemoryDB()` now returns a stub, and its `RunCommands` and `QueryFramesInto` methods always return "not implemented". As a result, three paths now fail unconditionally:
- `sql.TablesList`
- anything that relies on it, such as `NewSQLCommand`
- `SQLCommand.Execute`

Existing tests that assert parsed table names or successful SQL command execution will now fail. The test files are not in this diff, so check the repo to confirm which ones are affected.

Do one of the following for each affected test:
- remove it,
- mark it with `t.Skip`, or
- rewrite it to assert the not-implemented error.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
func TestTablesList_NotImplemented(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := sql.TablesList("select * from A")
	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "not implemented")
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Consensus: 1/3 reviewers
Title: Add a test for the new SQL rejection path in ReadQuery

Affected:
- pkg/expr/reader.go:128-132

Explanation:
The main behavior change is that `QueryTypeSQL` queries are now rejected at parse time, and no test covers it. Add a regression test that asserts `ReadQuery` returns the expected error both with and without `FlagSqlExpressions` enabled. This stops a future change from silently re-enabling the feature while the backend is still a stub.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
func TestReadQuery_SQLDisabled(t *testing.T) {
	for _, on := range []bool{true, false} {
		feats := featuremgmt.WithFeatures()
		if on {
			feats = featuremgmt.WithFeatures(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
		}
		r := NewExpressionQueryReader(feats)
		// build a "type":"sql" query and call r.ReadQuery(...)
		// require.Error(t, err)
	}
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Consensus: 3/3 reviewers
Title: Remove the unused stub `DB.TablesList` and the stale DuckDB-specific parsing code

Affected:
- pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-14
- pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:22-26

Explanation:
`DB.TablesList` is never called, because `parser.go` has its own package-level `TablesList`. That function still escapes quotes by hand and builds a DuckDB-specific `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` command. It then passes the command to a stub `RunCommands` that always fails.

The variable is also still named `duckDB`. This dead path suggests the parsing logic still works when it cannot.

The code also keeps SQL built by string interpolation, which could become live again if an engine is wired back in behind the same signature.

To fix:
- Short-circuit `TablesList` with a clear error.
- Remove the unused method.
- Document the stub type as a placeholder.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
// DB is a placeholder for the removed go-duck engine; all methods return ErrNotImplemented.
var ErrNotImplemented = errors.New("sql expressions engine not available")

func TablesList(rawSQL string) ([]string, error) {
	return nil, ErrNotImplemented
}
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Consensus: 2/3 reviewers
Title: Return a clear, typed error that says SQL expressions are disabled

Affected:
- pkg/expr/reader.go:129-132

Explanation:
Users who send a SQL expression get "sqlExpressions is not implemented", even if they have enabled the `sqlExpressions` toggle. That message does not tell them the flag is now ignored or that the feature is disabled.

The error is also an untyped `fmt.Errorf` with no format arguments, so it will likely surface as a generic internal error. Use an `errutil`-typed error, or at least `errors.New`, with a message that says the feature is disabled.

Proposed fix:
~~~go
var errSQLExpressionsDisabled = errutil.NotImplemented("sse.sqlDisabled").Errorf("SQL expressions are currently disabled")

case QueryTypeSQL:
	if !enableSqlExpressions(h) {
		return eq, errSQLExpressionsDisabled
	}
~~~
